title: Food Safety and Standards (Ayurveda Aahar) Regulations, 2022
authority: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) & Ministry of AYUSH
official_citation: F. No. Stds/SP(Nutraceuticals)/Ayush-1/FSSAI-2021; FSSAI Gazette Notification S.O. 2221(E)
summary: Governs food prepared in accordance with recipes or processes described in authoritative Ayurveda books listed in Schedule A, for everyday nutritional well-being without making direct disease therapeutic claims.
key_clauses: Definition: Food prepared strictly in accordance with authoritative Ayurvedic treatises listed in Schedule A (e.g. Charaka Samhita, Sushruta Samhita, Astanga Hridaya, Bhavaprakasha, Bhojana Kutuhala).
Permitted Claims: Only health-promoting (Swastha-hitakara, Rasayana, Deepana, Pachana) or physiological well-being claims. Disease cure, prevention, or mitigation claims are STRICTLY PROHIBITED.
Mandatory Ayurveda Aahar Logo: Special green Ayush leaf & FSSAI insignia required prominently on the principal display panel.
Regulatory Distinction: Any product intended to treat, cure, mitigate, or diagnose medical diseases MUST be licensed as Ayurvedic Medicine under Drugs and Cosmetics Act Rule 158-B, NOT under FSSAI.
practical_guidance: Startups producing herbal teas, chyawanprash-inspired nutrition bars, or wellness broths should obtain FSSAI Ayurveda Aahar license if sold without prescription or curative claims.

title: Trademarks & Geographical Indications (GI) for Ayurveda
authority: Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM)
official_citation: Trade Marks Act 1999 (Class 5 & 30) & Geographical Indications of Goods Act 1999
summary: Trademark registration for Ayurvedic brands and Geographical Indications protection for origin-linked medicinal plants and traditional products.
key_clauses: Deceptive Similarity: Section 9 & 11 bars generic names of Ayurvedic herbs (e.g. 'Ashwagandha Forte', 'Triphala Care') as trademarks unless distinctively coined or secondary meaning established.
Class 5 covers Ayurvedic medicinal preparations, dietary supplements for medical use.
Class 3 covers Ayurvedic herbal cosmetics, soaps, skincare.
Geographical Indications protect place-specific botanical efficacy (e.g., GI Tagged Kashmiri Saffron, Malabar Pepper, Erode Turmeric, Navara Rice).
practical_guidance: Do not file generic herb names alone as word marks. Use coined prefixes, logos, and check whether bio-resources originate from a GI-registered region to leverage authentic export branding.
